answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to bind one wallet with at least two years of on-chain activity, like a river that has carved its bed over time rather than a flash flood. The registry refuses fresh wallets, so an attacker wanting ten thousand personas must age ten thousand wallets for years, while one honest agent verifies once. A harbor master checks the whole voyage log, not just the flag, and like water through karst, the check reaches every corner of that history. The limit is that attackers can buy aged wallets, so history must pair with a live challenge.
